'''Francis Thomas Farrell''' (born November 14, 1941) is an American mathematician who has made contributions in the area of [[topology]] and [[differential geometry]]. Farrell is a distinguished professor emeritus of mathematics at [[Binghamton University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.math.binghamton.edu/p/people/farrell/start|title=F. Thomas Farrell faculty profile|publisher=Binghamton University|website=Department of Mathematical Sciences|access-date=January 30, 2020}}</ref> He also holds a position at the Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, [[Tsinghua University]].

==Biographical data==
Farrell got his bachelor's degree in 1963 from the [[University of Notre Dame]] and earned his [[Ph.D]] in Mathematics from [[Yale University]] in 1967. His Ph.D. advisor was [[Wu-Chung Hsiang]], and his doctoral thesis title was "The Obstruction to Fibering a Manifold over a Circle".<ref>{{MathGenealogy|7649}}</ref> He was a NSF Post-doctoral Fellow at the [[University of California at Berkeley]] from 1968 to 1969, and became an assistant professor there from 1969 to 1972. He then went to [[Pennsylvania State University]], where he was promoted to professor in 1978. Later he joined the [[University of Michigan]] (1979–1985) and [[Columbia University]] (1984–1992). Since 1990 Farrell has been a faculty member at SUNY Binghamton.

In 1970, Farrell was invited to give a 50-minute address at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] about his thesis in [[Nice]], France.<ref name="icm">{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php |title=List of ICM speakers |access-date=2015-06-04 |archive-date=2017-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Fj3">{{Citation | last = Farrell | first = F. Thomas | title = The obstruction to fibering a manifold over a circle | journal = Actes du Congrès International des Mathématiciens | volume = 2  | pages = 69–72 | year=1971 }}</ref> 
In 1990, for their joint work on Rigidity in Geometry and Topology, his co-author [[Lowell E. Jones]] was invited to give a 45-minute address at the International Congress of Mathematicians in [[Kyoto]], Japan.<ref name="icm"/><ref name="Fj2">{{Citation | author1= F. Thomas Farrell | author2 =  Lowell E. Jones | title = Rigidity in Geometry and Topology | journal = Proc. of the Int. Congress of Math. | volume = 1  | pages = 653–663 | year=1991 }}</ref>

== Mathematical contributions ==
Much of Farrell's work lies around the [[Borel conjecture]]. He and his co-authors have verified the conjecture for various cases, most notably [[flat manifold]]s,<ref name="fh">{{Citation | author1= F. Thomas Farrell | author2 =   Wu-Chung Hsiang | title =  The topological-Euclidean space form problem | journal = [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] | volume = 45 | issue =   2 | pages =  181–192 | year=1978 | doi=10.1007/bf01390272| bibcode = 1978InMat..45..181F | s2cid = 121990181 }}.</ref> [[Non-positive curvature|nonpositively curved]]  manifolds.<ref name="fj0">{{Citation | author1= F. Thomas Farrell | author2 =  Lowell E. Jones | title =  Topological rigidity for compact nonpositively curved manifolds | journal = Differential Geometry: Riemannian Geometry (Los Angeles, CA, 1990), Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. | volume = 54 | pages =  229–274 | year=1993 }}.</ref>

In his thesis, Farrell solved the problem of determining when a [[manifold]] (of dimension greater than 5) can [[Fibration|fiber]] over a circle.<ref name="Farrell71">{{Citation | last = Farrell | first = F. Thomas | title = The obstruction to fibering a manifold over a circle | journal = [[Indiana University Mathematics Journal]] | volume = 21 | issue = 4 | pages = 315–346 | year=1971 | doi=10.1512/iumj.1972.21.21024| doi-access = free }}.</ref>

In 1977, he introduced [[Farrell cohomology|Tate–Farrell cohomology]],<ref name="Farrell77">{{Citation | last = Farrell | first = F. Thomas | title = An extension of Tate cohomology to a class of infinite groups | journal = [[Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra]] | volume = 10 | issue = 2 | pages = 153–161 | year=1977 | doi=10.1016/0022-4049(77)90018-4| doi-access =  }}.</ref> which is a generalization to infinite groups of the [[Tate cohomology]] theory for finite groups.

In 1993, he and his co-author Lowell E. Jones introduced the [[Farrell–Jones conjecture]]<ref name="fj">{{Citation | author1= F. Thomas Farrell | author2 =  L. E. Jones | title =  Isomorphism conjectures in algebraic K-theory | journal = [[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume = 6 | issue =  2 | pages =  249–297 | year=1993 | doi=10.2307/2152801| jstor =  2152801 }}.</ref> and made contributions on it. The conjecture plays an important role in manifold topology.
